kente-weaver.intro: Learn Kente weaving from Ghana and the wider West African strip-cloth tradition. Master the loom, the patterns, the cultural meanings, and the business of selling one of Africa's most recognised textiles.

skillDomains.name: Loom Work
skillDomains.description: The physical skill of the loom — warping, weaving, and maintaining the equipment.

skills.name: Loom Setup
skills.description: Prepare the loom correctly. Bad setup ruins hours of weaving.

modules.title: The Kente loom
modules.content:
Traditional Kente is woven on a horizontal narrow-strip loom. The weaver sits at one end, controlling the heddles with their feet while throwing the shuttle by hand.

The loom produces strips about 10–12cm wide. Many strips are later sewn together to make full cloths.

Key parts

  • Heddles — raise and lower warp threads
  • Shuttle — carries the weft thread
  • Beater — packs each weft thread tight
  • Warp beam — holds tension on the warp threads

modules.title: Warping — the foundation
modules.content:
Warping is preparing the lengthwise threads. It takes hours, and it determines everything about the finished cloth.

Steps

  1. Measure the warp threads to the required length (usually 3–4 metres per strip)
  2. Wind them onto a warping frame or posts in the correct colour order
  3. Transfer to the loom and tie to the warp beam under even tension
  4. Thread through the heddles in the pattern sequence

Uneven tension = wavy cloth. Wrong colour order = pattern ruined. Warping is not rushed.

steps.q: You need to weave a strip 12cm wide and 3.5m long. What do you prepare first?
o: The warp — correct width and length
steps.f: Every strip starts with warping. Always.

steps.q: Halfway through warping, you notice tension is uneven. What do you do?
steps.f: Restart. Uneven warp produces a permanently wavy, unusable strip.

steps.q: Your finished cloth has a slight ripple on one side. Most likely cause?
steps.f: Ripples almost always trace back to warping.

skills.name: Weaving Technique
skills.description: Pass the shuttle, pack the weft, build the cloth.

modules.title: The weave itself
modules.content:
Weaving is simple in principle:

  1. Lift the heddles to raise alternate warp threads
  2. Throw the shuttle through the gap (called the shed)
  3. Beat the weft thread tight against the previous one
  4. Switch the heddles and repeat

Every inch of cloth is hundreds of these cycles. Skilled weavers work rhythmically, almost unconsciously. The rhythm is what makes good cloth.

steps.q: You notice your weft threads are packed unevenly. Result?
steps.f: Uneven beating leaves gaps. The cloth looks poor and wears badly.

steps.q: The shuttle keeps catching on warp threads. What do you do?
o: Check the shed (gap) is fully open
steps.f: A properly opened shed lets the shuttle pass freely. If it's catching, the heddles aren't lifting fully.

steps.q: You want to change colour mid-strip. What do you do?
o: Cut the weft and start the new colour, tucking the ends in later
steps.f: Cut the weft, start the new colour. Tuck ends during finishing. Never knot — knots show.

skillDomains.name: Pattern Knowledge
skillDomains.description: Kente is a language of named patterns. Learn the vocabulary.

skills.name: Pattern Families
skills.description: The named patterns and their meanings.

modules.title: Named patterns
modules.content:
Kente patterns are named. Each name carries a proverb or meaning.

Examples

  • Adweneasa — "my skill is exhausted". The most complex pattern, with no plain background.
  • Sika futuro — "gold dust". Wealth and prosperity.
  • Emaa da — "it has not happened before". Novelty and uniqueness.
  • Obaa ko dua — "a woman weaves a good cloth". Skill and craftsmanship.

The pattern choice signals the occasion and the wearer's intent.

steps.q: A wedding commission. Which pattern family?
steps.f: Sika futuro (gold dust) is used for weddings — wealth and prosperity.

steps.q: A graduation gift for a first-in-family graduate. Best pattern?
steps.f: Emaa da ("it has not happened before") suits a first-time achievement.

steps.q: A commission showcasing your finest work. Which pattern?
steps.f: Adweneasa ("my skill is exhausted") is the weaver's showcase pattern.

modules.title: Advise a client
modules.prompt: A client is commissioning a Kente cloth for their mother's 70th birthday. They don't know the patterns. Write a message explaining three pattern options you would recommend and why.
modules.context: Educating clients about pattern meaning is how you sell more than just cloth.

Explains each meaning in plain language

Suggests colours that suit the occasion

skillDomains.name: Colour
skillDomains.description: Colour in Kente is not decoration. It carries meaning.

skills.name: Colour Meaning
skills.description: The symbolic weight of each colour.

modules.title: Kente colour vocabulary
modules.content:
• Gold — royalty, wealth, spiritual purity
  • Green — growth, harvest, renewal
  • Blue — peacefulness, harmony, love
  • Red — political passion, sacrifice, spiritual intensity
  • Black — maturity, spiritual strength, ancestral connection
  • White — purification, festive occasions, prayer
  • Purple — femininity, healing, care

A cloth's colour story matters as much as its pattern.

steps.q: A funeral cloth for an elder. Which colour dominant?
steps.f: Black for ancestral connection, red for the gravity of the occasion.

steps.q: A wedding cloth. Which colour palette?
steps.f: Gold (wealth, joy) and blue (love, harmony) suit weddings.

steps.q: A cloth for a newborn naming ceremony. Which colour?
steps.f: White (purity, new beginning) and green (growth) suit new life.

skillDomains.name: Cultural Meaning
skillDomains.description: Kente is not just cloth. It is history woven into fabric.

skills.name: History & Origins
skills.description: Where Kente comes from and what it represents.

modules.title: The origins of Kente
modules.content:
Kente originates with the Asante and Ewe peoples of Ghana and Togo. Asante tradition holds that the craft was inspired by a spider's web observed by two weavers, who reproduced the pattern for the Asantehene (king).

For centuries, Kente was royal — worn by kings and court officials on important occasions. Specific patterns were reserved for specific ranks.

Today Kente is worn for graduations, weddings, funerals, and celebrations around the world. It has become a global symbol of African identity.

Being a Kente weaver means carrying this history forward.

modules.title: Explain Kente to a foreign buyer
modules.prompt: A European boutique wants to stock your Kente. They ask what makes it special. Write a short explanation (under 200 words) that is culturally accurate, respectful, and commercially compelling.
modules.context: Export clients pay more when they understand what they're buying. Education is a sales skill.
rubric: Explains that patterns are named and carry meaning
Notes that colours have symbolic value
Explains the weaving process briefly (strip loom, hand-woven)
Positions Kente as both heritage and contemporary
Ends with what makes your cloth distinct

skillDomains.name: Business
skillDomains.description: Weaving is a craft. Selling is a business.

skills.name: Pricing Kente
skills.description: Price for the time and skill Kente requires.

modules.title: Kente is slow work
modules.content:
A full Kente cloth can take weeks to months to weave. A single strip can take hours. The price must reflect this.

The four-part price

  1. Materials — thread, dye, and wear on the loom
  2. Labour — your hours, at a real rate
  3. Overhead — workshop, tools, electricity, transport
  4. Margin — the profit that keeps you in business

Tourists often expect "African craft" prices. That expectation is wrong. Kente is luxury textile work. Price it accordingly.

modules.title: Price a full Kente cloth
modules.prompt: A client orders a full Kente cloth (24 strips) for a graduation. Materials cost 180,000 Le. You estimate 60 hours of weaving time at 4,000 Le/hour. Overhead is 20,000 Le. You want a 45% margin. Calculate the price.
modules.context: Kente buyers often don't understand the labour involved. Your price must reflect reality, not expectation.
